console.title: GAWorld Twin Console
console.description: Configuration, agents, simulation, interviews, and memory observation — all in one local panel.
sim.fast_forward_hint: Long-run fast-forward: compress each step into one brief (one LLM call per agent per step), skipping the intra-day tick loop; state/goals/relationships still evolve approximately. How much time a step covers is set by Step unit next to it — Day suits 60/600-day horizons, Month or Year are what make multi-year runs feasible.
sim.step_unit_hint: How much time one fast-forward step covers: a day (one brief per agent per day), a month, or a year. Multi-year horizons need month or year — otherwise the call count grows linearly with the number of days. Only applies in fast-forward mode.
sim.randomness_hint: Randomness: higher means more frequent sudden (burst) events and larger day-to-day swings during fast-forward. 0 = fully deterministic (no bursts, no jitter). Only applies in fast-forward mode.
sim.routine_randomness_hint: Routine randomness: higher means agents follow their daily routine less — deviating from scheduled activities and their plan more often. 0 = strictly follow the schedule (sleep slots are unaffected).
sim.scheduled: Scheduled: the run starts automatically at {at}
btn.schedule_run_hint: Schedule a run: at the time you set, the server starts the simulation with the current config. The time is the local clock of the machine running the dashboard, and closing this page does not cancel it.

agent.ids_hint: Resident IDs taking part in the simulation, comma-separated (e.g. 1,2,3). A single number N means the first N residents.
agent.profile_title_hint: This resident's profile (read-only). To change it, go to Agent Studio.
agent.roster_hint: Avatars of the residents in this run (from Agent IDs above). Click an avatar to see that resident's profile.
analytics.behavior_hint: Where residents actually went, their travel mode preferences, a habit-strength heatmap accumulated by time slot × context, and the time distribution of scheduled activities.
analytics.economy_hint: The day-by-day ledger from output/economy: assets, income and spending, savings, and investment over time, plus the final wealth ranking and macro cycle state. Resident filtering follows the selection in the state section above.
analytics.events_hint: A timeline laid out in swim lanes by event type, with dot size showing event intensity. Compare it against the state curves above to see how event shocks affect residents.
analytics.export_csv_note: Split table by table; imports into Excel / pandas
analytics.export_html_note: All charts included; opens offline or prints to PDF
analytics.export_json_note: Exactly as the API returns it, for further analysis
analytics.export_md_note: Written conclusions to paste into a paper or weekly report
analytics.headline: Simulation Result Analysis
analytics.hero_sub: State changes · Economic trajectories · Social networks · Behavior distributions · Event timelines
analytics.meta_description: GAWorld simulation result visualization: state changes, economic trajectories, social networks, behavior distributions, and event timelines
analytics.overview_hint: The scale of what this simulation produced, plus the state metrics that moved most (ranked by the mean first-to-last change across all agents). Use the selector at the top of the page to switch which run you are analyzing: the current run, an archived run, or a scenario comparison run.
analytics.social_hint: Large dots are residents in the simulation; small dots are background ties such as relatives and acquaintances. Line thickness shows closeness and color depth shows trust. Hover for exact values.
analytics.state_hint: One line chart per metric: the horizontal axis is the simulation sampling step, the vertical axis is the state value normalized to [0,1], and each line is one resident. Below are the first-to-last comparison and the final state radar.
btn.all_settings_hint: Open the settings center: every configuration option in this project lives there, each one documented.
collab.deck: Group residents, assign roles, and watch a real collaboration unfold along the plan, activity, and artifact tracks.

docs.sub_before: What you see here is the documentation in the repository's
external.headline: Watch the world itself, not just the people living in it
external.meta_description: GAWorld external systems observatory: currency system · external environment · outbound services
external.sub: How money moves, what events the environment throws out, whether outbound services are reachable — observe them, then change them directly.
external.tab_currency_hint: How money moves through this world: the macro picture, the corporate/government/bank pools, whether the total is conserved, and how wealth is distributed. You can also change the economic rules here, or intervene once in a running simulation.
external.tab_environment_hint: What happens in the world each day: weather, economic news, policy, technology. These events enter every resident's daily context and shape their mood and schedule.
external.tab_services_hint: Everywhere the simulation dials out to: the external environment service, multi-machine relays, news sources, and which large model is used. You can check reachability here and change it.
fos_export.title_hint: Export the analysis prompt for FOS AI Scientist, handing this run's results to the research analysis pipeline (optionally with an English summary).
interview.title_hint: Ask the selected resident a question; the model answers with their profile and memory as background. One question per line, with optional context.
life_event.title_hint: Inject a life event (job loss, relocation, bereavement) into one or more residents and watch their state and behavior shift over the rest of the simulation.
memory.title_hint: The selected resident's long-term memory, schedule/habits/intentions, recent episodes, and agent log. "Raw Data" lets you view and download the unprocessed JSON / JSONL / log text.
population.checkup_hint: A purely mathematical check — it generates no people and updates live as you move the sliders. When parameters contradict each other it tells you which one to change.
population.headline: Build a small town, then let it run
population.meta_description: GAWorld population generation and cohort simulation studio
population.step1_hint: Pick a population template, then set the size and random seed
population.step2_hint: Set age, household, employment, and income, then generate the cohort
population.step3_hint: Set residents' emotion, stress, sense of security, and other psychological state
population.step4_hint: Simulate by cohort for a number of days, choosing which model to use
population.step5_hint: Use a controlled experiment to check whether this approximation holds up
population.sub: Set the population structure → generate a few hundred residents → run a low-cost cohort simulation → check whether the results hold up. You can try the whole thing without spending anything.
run_log.title_hint: Live output from the background simulation process, for tracking progress and diagnosing errors.
settings.headline: Every knob in one place — know what it does before you turn it
settings.meta_description: GAWorld settings center: view and change every simulation, model, environment, and economy option in one place
settings.only_overridden_hint: Show only options whose current value differs from the code default — the ones overridden by dashboard_config.json, an environment variable, or environment_config.json. Answers "what did this run actually change?" quickly.
settings.search_placeholder: Search options by name, path, or description, e.g. inflation / sim_days / memory
settings.sub: All configuration options live here. Hover any one of them to see what it does, what the default is, and where the current value came from.
sim.days_hint: How many days this simulation runs.
sim.months_hint: How many calendar months the run covers (converted to sim days on the real calendar). With the step unit set to Month, one month is one step.
sim.years_hint: How many calendar years the run covers (converted to sim days on the real calendar, leap years included). With the step unit set to Year, one year is one step.
sim.default_llm_hint: The language model provider agents use by default for thinking, acting, and interviews.
sim.schedule_llm_hint: The language model used to generate daily schedules (can differ from the default to save cost).
sim.seconds_per_day_hint: Real seconds per simulated day: larger values mean finer within-day steps and slower replay.
sim.time_step_hint: Granularity of within-day progression: leave empty for the default, or enter 60 (seconds) or "2 hours".
studio.headline: Build a digital resident
studio.headline_hint: Agent Studio: design and deploy a city resident with state, memory, social ties, and goals across seven steps — Identity → State & Personality → Abilities & Skills → Memory → Social & Relationships → Behavior & Goals → Review & Deploy. Switch between existing residents on the left.
studio.meta_description: GAWorld agent showcase and editing studio
studio.pick_agent_hint: Pick the resident to view or edit and the form on the right loads their settings; or click "＋ New" at the top right to create one.
studio.sub: Design generative city resident agents with state, memory, social ties, and goals.
trace.frame_json_hint: Raw simulation data for the current moment (JSON): the frame's day, time, and date, plus each agent's position, state, and current activity — for development and debugging.
trace.not_loaded_hint: Live trace replay: shows each resident's position and state in the city, frame by frame. Drag the timeline to revisit any frame, or check "Follow latest" to track the newest frame.
worlds.branch_hint: The horizontal axis is simulated days. Every world starts on the same trunk and forks at its first event; the thickness after the fork shows how far it has drifted from the baseline.
worlds.deltas_hint: Each world's final-value and mean differences relative to the baseline world, sorted by absolute difference.
worlds.divergence_hint: At each step, the mean absolute difference across all of this world's metrics versus the baseline world at the same step. The step where it first stably crosses the threshold is the moment the two histories genuinely part.
worlds.headline: Same people, one different event — watch history fork
worlds.list_hint: Each world is a full simulation with its own memory, log, and state directory. Add an event to a world and it walks a different history; a world with no event is the baseline.
worlds.meta_description: GAWorld parallel worlds lab: change an event, compare how different worlds unfold
worlds.movers_hint: The final gap for the same resident across two worlds. Population means flatten individual variation; this table brings it back.
worlds.readout: Hover the chart to read the value at a given step.
worlds.relative: Show only the gap from baseline
worlds.setup_hint: These settings are identical across every parallel world: same residents, same number of days, same random seed. Keeping them fixed is what lets you attribute the final differences to the event itself.
worlds.sub: Every world shares the same residents, the same random seed, and the same model. The only difference is what happened. Whatever diverges is what that event caused.
worlds.trajectory_hint: Each line is one world's population mean for that metric over time. Dashed lines mark where events occur.

simviz.run_hint: Pick which simulation run to replay: the current run is the live trace still being written; historical runs are archived automatically after each run; scenario/comparison runs come from separate output directories such as compare-event.
simviz.run_select_title: Select which simulation run to replay
simviz.insight_hint: Shows what each agent is doing and thinking in the current frame, in sync with playback. Click any card to expand that agent's full mental chain: perception → thought → action → outcome → reflection.
simviz.live_poll_hint: When on, polls for the newest simulation data and refreshes the replay; when off, stays on the frames already loaded.
simviz.details_title: Show/hide the actions and thoughts panel

village.headline: Pixel Village · Generative Agent Replay
village.sub: Top-down village, overhead bubbles, activity scene cards; buildings are laid out automatically from citymap nodes.
village.timeline_hint: Drag the timeline to see what agents are doing around town.
family.title: Households
family.title_hint: Who is married, who lives with whom, and who they look after.
family.empty: No household data yet — run a full simulation and each resident's family shows up here.
family.not_in_run: This resident was not part of the last run, so there is no household record.
